findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are embedded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, making them readable to anyone with DescribeInstances/DescribeInstanceAttribute permission and exposing long-lived static credentials.
No metadata_options block is set to require IMDSv2 (http_tokens = required), leaving the legacy instance metadata service enabled and vulnerable to SSRF-based credential theft.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF/ALB), broadening the direct internet-facing attack surface on the instance itself.
Egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing unrestricted outbound traffic and a potential data exfiltration or command-and-control channel.
The EBS volume does not enable encryption (encrypted attribute is commented out), leaving data at rest unprotected.
The EBS snapshot inherits from an unencrypted source volume and has no encryption configured, exposing data at rest in the snapshot.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances in this subnet, increasing internet-facing exposure for workloads that may not require it.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances in this subnet, increasing internet-facing exposure for workloads that may not require it.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking exposure of sensitive network traffic logs.
